# Sirach Chapter 18 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 18 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_018_page_001.jpg

---

**18:1** The one who lives forever created the entire universe;

**18:2** the LORD alone is truly righteous.

**18:3** He holds the world in the span of his hand; all things obey his will. He is king over everything by his power, separating the sacred from the ordinary among them.

**18:4** No one has been given the power to declare what he has done; who could possibly trace his mighty acts?

**18:5** Who could measure the immensity of his majesty? Who could stretch out their hand and recount all his acts of mercy?

**18:6** Nothing can be subtracted from it or added; it is not possible to plumb the wonders of the LORD.

**18:7** When a human being thinks they've finished, they've barely begun; when they stop, they're only confused.

**18:8** What is a human being, anyway? What good are they? What is their strength and what is their weakness?

**18:9** A human life runs a hundred years at best —

**18:10** like a drop of water in an ocean, a single grain of sand on a beach: that's how our brief years compare to eternity.

**18:11** This is why the LORD is patient with people, pouring out his mercy on them.

**18:12** He sees and knows that their end will be bad — and so he multiplies his forgiveness all the more.

**18:13** Human compassion reaches only as far as the next person; but the LORD's compassion reaches all flesh. He corrects, trains, teaches, and brings people back — like a shepherd with his flock.

**18:14** He shows compassion to those who accept correction and who seek his decrees with zeal.

**18:15** My child, don't mix criticism in with your good deeds, or bitter words with any gift you give.

**18:16** Doesn't dew cool the heat? Just so, a kind word is worth more than a gift.

**18:17** Isn't a good word worth more than the best gift? And yet both together are what you find in a truly gracious person.

**18:18** A fool is graceless and insulting; a gift from someone who resents giving it makes your eyes water.

**18:19** Before you speak, learn; before you get sick, look after your health.

**18:20** Before the judgment comes, examine your own conscience; when the moment of reckoning arrives, you will find forgiveness.

**18:21** Before you fall ill, humble yourself; when you've sinned, show that you're truly sorry.

**18:22** Don't let anything stop you from paying a vow when it's due; don't put it off until you're dying.

**18:23** Before you make a vow, be prepared; and don't be the kind of person who tests God.

**18:24** Think about the wrath that is coming at the end — the hour of punishment when God turns his face away.

**18:25** In good times, think about bad times; in times of wealth, think about poverty and want.

**18:26** Conditions can change from one morning to the next; before the LORD, everything moves quickly.

**18:27** The wise person is careful in everything; in bad times, they're doubly on guard against foolishness.

**18:28** Every intelligent person can recognize wisdom — and gives honor to the one who found her.

**18:29** Those who understand wise sayings have themselves become wise; they pour out fitting proverbs.

**18:30** Don't follow after your cravings — keep your appetites in check.

**18:31** Give your soul everything it wants and you'll end up a joke in the eyes of your enemies.

**18:32** Don't indulge in luxury — it could leave you bankrupt.

**18:33** Don't throw feasts on borrowed money when your own purse is empty — that's how you end up a beggar.
